A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same model-stitching study. Their complete main text, Appendices A-J, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite the revised title and notation.

before.justification: v1 reports original stitching losses, SAE training-efficiency measurements, probing and steering experiments, and feature analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results on model stitching, SAE transfer and training, probing, steering, and semantic, structural, and functional features.

M1.justification: The bidirectional affine stitches, reconstruction-plus-inversion objective, SVCCA layer selection, SAE parameter transfer, and probing and steering procedures are unchanged. Revised activation notation does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenWebText, eight SAEBench probing datasets, EuroParl language steering, IFEval instruction-following tasks, and synthetic semantic/structural sentence augmentations. No dataset, domain, language, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: scratch versus transferred SAE initialization; ground-truth, random-feature, and dense probes; and unsteered, native-steered, and transfer-steered models. Appendix comparisons also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Previously stated model-layer pairs, training budgets, context lengths, probing settings, steering procedures, and metrics remain unchanged. Appendix A newly discloses the evaluation sample selection for an existing experiment; it does not report a revised protocol or new experiment.

E4.justification: The inversion-strength ablation, initialization analysis, language-frequency analysis, semantic/structural comparisons, and entropy and attention-feature case studies are retained with the same evidence, including the supplementary analyses in Appendices A and D-I.

E5.justification: Both versions specify Clopper-Pearson intervals at alpha = 0.05 in Appendix F and retain the steering confidence intervals and error bars. No seed information, repeat counts, or statistical estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and experimental plots retain their results and trends. Examples include Pythia A-to-B cross-entropy loss of 3.99 in Table 1, Gemma original/transferred SAE FUV of 0.21/0.42 in Table 2, and the reported 30-50% SAE-training FLOP savings.

T1.justification: The affine transfer formulas, SAE-transfer derivation, attribution-correlation definition, and approximate scaling-law equations are mathematically unchanged. Renaming activation variables and explicitly stating matrix dimensions clarify existing mathematics without changing the reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the explicit aim of addressing the Linear Representation Hypothesis's faithfulness and instead presents shared linear representations as a working premise. The contribution summary and conclusion explicitly invoke weak universality, while the substantive efficiency and feature-transfer claims remain intact.

C2.justification: The explanations and limitations remain substantively unchanged, including rank-limited transfer, same-family/tokenizer restrictions, incomplete scaling-law fits, and chat-token and sample-noise explanations for weak instruction steering. The weak-universality interpretation was already present in v1's Sections 2-3.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies evaluation on the next 1,000 OpenWebText samples after the 180,000 training samples, using the same context lengths. Table 1 also explicitly identifies OpenWebText. These additions improve documentation without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 6 are unchanged. However, the introduction modestly repositions the relationship to the Linear Representation Hypothesis: v1 aims to address its faithfulness, whereas v3 treats the shared-linear-representation premise as an ansatz supporting the transfer application.

P1.justification: v3 adds 'Linear' to the title, expands the introductory explanation of superposition and SAEs, revises contribution wording, and standardizes activation notation. Affiliation, conference-footer, and acknowledgment disclosures also change. Section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's schematic is relabeled and slightly rearranged to match the revised notation, and its caption is edited. Table 1's caption adds the evaluation dataset. The existing figures and tables are retained, with limited typesetting and text-flow changes.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves reproducibility by documenting the held-out evaluation samples in Appendix A and improves clarity by distinguishing activation variables from layer indices and refining the introductory framing. The methods, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged, so the gains are useful but limited.
